codeReviewIssues.description: SharedHttpClient is a static readonly singleton, so Dispose(bool) only sets the _disposed flag without releasing any managed resources. This is correct for a shared static HttpClient, but the Dispose pattern is somewhat ceremonial — consider documenting why Dispose doesn't actually release the HttpClient (to avoid confusion for future maintainers).

Lines 127-175: Uses manual try/finally with explicit client.Dispose() instead of the 'using' pattern used in NegotiationManager (line 782) and SocialInteractions.GenerateTextWithApiClient (line 2123). Functionally equivalent but stylistically inconsistent. The manual pattern is justified here since the client is created inside Task.Run and the try/finally spans async operations.

UpdatePlayer2Heartbeat (lines 51-71) references concrete Player2ApiClient.StartHealthHeartbeat/StopHealthHeartbeat static methods directly. This is acceptable since the factory is in Api/ and heartbeat is a Player2-specific non-ILlmClient concern, but it does mean LlmClientFactory has knowledge of Player2-specific static members beyond the interface contract.

summary: All 17 validation contract assertions (VAL-API-001 through VAL-API-017) are satisfied. The refactoring correctly extracts ILlmClient interface (with GenerateText + Name + IDisposable), LlmClientBase abstract class (with shared HttpClient, POST logic, error handling that returns null and logs via SLog), and LlmClientFactory (handling all 10 LlmApiType values with correct constructor parameter diversity). All 10 API clients extend LlmClientBase and are no longer static. Callers outside Api/ (SocialInteractions.GenerateTextWithApiClient, NegotiationManager.GetLLMResponse, JobDriver_HaveDeepTalk) use LlmClientFactory/ILlmClient. No HttpClient usage for LLM outside Api/. Provider-specific request building is preserved in each client's BuildRequestBody/ExtractText/CreateRequestMessage/BuildRequestUrl overrides. Build and tests pass. Three non-blocking style/documentation observations noted.
